subject: Phased onboarding & incentive structure — pricing alignment for evaluation ramp
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Phased onboarding & incentive structure — pricing alignment for evaluation ramp

Alex — thanks for taking the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a concise Mutual Action Plan (Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx) that ties the evaluation milestones to commercial checkpoints and discounts. High level:  

- Evaluation window: 30 days (pilot) followed by a 3-month ramp if metrics met.
- Checkpoints: Day 10 (initial results), Day 20 (stability), Day 30 (go/no-go).
- Pricing mechanics: pilot-rate with an introductory "Pilot Discount" applied to usage during the 30-day evaluation, followed by tiered discounts tied to committed monthly throughput at the 3-month mark.
- Example incentive: sign MAP + 6-month ramp commitment -> additional tranche-based discounts at 6/12 month commit levels.

I've also included a short set of pricing variants in the spreadsheet so you can see trade-offs (higher upfront commit vs more aggressive early discounts). Main asks: confirm procurement timeline, whether Acme needs a PO or SOW for the pilot, and which internal stakeholders to include for legal review.

If this looks right, we'll finalize a MAP and circulate a one-page commercial summary for procurement.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0199

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-25T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Phased onboarding & incentive structure — pricing alignment for evaluation ramp

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap and the MAP file. A couple of questions from our side:  

1) Pilot discount: Can you tighten the pilot discount to be more material? Our procurement wants to see a clear delta between pilot and production pricing (we were hoping for ~30% off list during the 30-day pilot).
2) Commitment cadence: Would Acme be able to get a more aggressive mid-ramp discount if we hit certain usage thresholds earlier (e.g., hit 60% of target in month 2)?
3) Procurement: We will need a one-page commercial summary for our vendor committee and a draft SOW to attach to the PO. Can you confirm lead time for those?

Procurement note (procurement@acme.com): Our standard review calendar is next Tuesday (2026-12-01). If we can have the one-pager and pricing schedule before then, procurement can queue this for review.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Platforms, Acme Corp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Phased onboarding & incentive structure — pricing alignment for evaluation ramp

Alex — appreciate the clarity. We can do a stronger pilot concession with two paths to choose from. Attached: pricing-variants-20261125.pdf (short doc) — summary below:  

Variant A — "Aggressive Pilot":
- Pilot (30 days): 30% off list for tokens + waived onboarding fees.
- Post-pilot: If Acme commits to a 3-month ramp and meets 60% of target by month 2, an incremental 10% discount applies retroactively to months 2–3.

Variant B — "Phased Commitment":
- Pilot (30 days): 20% off list.
- Post-pilot: Step-down discounts at 3/6/12 months keyed to committed monthly spend; stronger discounts if a 6-month minimum revenue commit is signed (up to 35% at scale).

We can provide the one-page commercial summary and an SOW template within 48 business hours. For procurement's 12/01 review cycle, Variant A will require an internal approval for the aggressive pilot concession — worth noting.

If you prefer, Lauren can propose a constrained approval path (e.g., capped pilot discount applied only to first $X of usage) so legal/procurement can approve faster.

Next step: let us know which variant you'd prefer and whether procurement needs the SOW redline ahead of 12/01.

Thanks — Jordan

Attachments: pricing-variants-20261125.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: approval guidance for Acme pilot concessions

Jordan / Lauren — quick decision: I reviewed the variant options and approve Variant A (Aggressive Pilot) under the following guardrails:  

- Pilot discount up to 30% off list, limited to the first $25k of billable usage during the 30-day evaluation. Any overage billed at standard pilot rate.
- Post-pilot discounts are contingent on a signed MAP + a 6-month ramp commitment (minimum committed spend to be defined in the one-page commercial summary).
- Legal should fast-track SOW (we can accept our standard SOW with a short redline for the capped pilot clause).
- Please require procurement to confirm PO timing; if procurement cannot meet 12/01, we'll maintain pilot pricing for 7 calendar days after procurement approval but reserve the right to pull concession after that window.

Lauren — please draft the one-page commercial summary reflecting the cap and the conditional post-pilot discounts. Jordan — confirm back to Acme once the doc is ready so they can attach for the vendor committee.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Phased onboarding & incentive structure — pricing alignment for evaluation ramp

Jordan / Marissa — this works for us. Acme accepts Variant A under the cap you described (pilot concession applied up to $25k during the 30-day evaluation). We'll present the one-page summary and the draft SOW to Vendor Committee on 2026-12-01. Procurement will confirm PO timing after that meeting — likely the week of 2026-12-07.

Next steps for Redwood: please circulate the finalized one-pager and SOW redline today/tomorrow so procurement can include it in the Vendor Committee packet. If legal needs to touch the SOW, our counsel (Samantha Lee) will coordinate redlines the same day.

We'll plan to run the pilot starting the week after PO issuance; Alex will confirm exact kick date once procurement has the final doc.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting started.

—Alex

Attachments: signed_intent.pdf (signed intent to proceed, lightweight)
